jobs.description:

$147,151.48 - $200,000.00

This position is bonus and/or commission eligible.

CCC Intelligent Solutions Inc. (CCC) is a leading cloud platform for the multi-trillion-dollar insurance economy ,
creating intelligent experiences for insurers, repairers, automakers, part suppliers, and more. At CCC, we’re making life just work by empowering more than 35,000 businesses with industry-leading technology to get drivers back on the road and to health quickly and seamlessly. We’re pushing boundaries with innovative AI solutions that simplify and enhance the claims and repair journey. Through purposeful innovation and the strength of its connections, CCC technologies empower the people and industry relied upon to keep lives moving forward when it matters most. Learn more about CCC at www.cccis.com.

The Role

CCC is seeking a Principal Product Manager for our Outbound Subrogation product, one of the most consequential and underserved categories in the insurance economy. More than $30 billion flows through subrogation workflows every year, yet most carriers are still operating on outdated, manual processes. This role will have the opportunity to bring subrogation into the AI era, with an unprecedented scale of impact.

We are relaunching this product in 2027 with the ambition of building it into a category-defining platform. You will define the product strategy, own the roadmap, shape the architecture alongside engineering and data science, and be the expert in the room when carriers evaluate what to buy. You will work with a dedicated set of development pods, significant autonomy, and close partnership with senior product leadership. This role starts as an individual contributor with a clear path to building and growing your team as the product scales.

Key Responsibilities:

Own and drive the product roadmap for Outbound Subrogation user experience, including prioritization of features, data capabilities, AI enhancements, and integrations
Translate market signals, customer research, and competitive intelligence into a clear, defensible strategy you can articulate from the carrier floor to the executive team
Set and track the metrics that matter to carriers: dollars recovered, identification rate, cycle time, and other ROI signals. Be accountable for moving them.
Partner with data science and engineering on topics from architecture for next-best-action and workflow design to how LLM-based capabilities like explainability are deployed and governed
Conduct customer research with recovery managers, subrogation adjusters, and carrier teams; get concepts in front of real users and make hard product decisions based on what you find
Represent the voice of the user in every internal product and prioritization conversation; maintain a continuous feedback loop between the field and the roadmap
Contribute directly to working software alongside engineers, using AI coding tools as a part of how you work - not only a manager delegating a spec, but as a builder participating in the work
Build and own the ROI case for the product: define how carriers measure value from subrogation tooling and hold the product accountable to those measures
Partner with sales, customer success, and product marketing on go-to-market execution, sales enablement materials, and carrier-facing ROI narratives
Support active sales cycles as the product expert: show up in carrier conversations and help close deals by articulating value credibly to buyer stakeholders from operations leads to C-suite

Requirements:

6+ years of product management experience in enterprise software or high-growth SaaS (preferred); Principal designation will be determined based on scope and experience
At least one 0-to-1 product build or major relaunch in a startup or high-velocity environment
Demonstrated experience building and shipping AI-driven or data-intensive products with LLMs, scoring models, or ML pipelines as core components
Track record of working directly with enterprise customers and senior stakeholders to validate product direction, plan for and track adoption, and support commercial outcomes
Deep experience in at least one complex, regulated vertical (insurance, fintech, healthtech, legaltech, or similar); direct subrogation or claims experience is a meaningful differentiator
Comfort operating in ambiguity, with a bias toward action and learning over extensive upfront planning

Even Better If You

You are a product professional who has built and shipped a product with meaningful business outcomes. You have owned a roadmap, shipped features that changed what customers could do, made hard prioritization calls, and operated as the connective tissue between engineering, data science, customers, and commercial teams, often simultaneously.
You have built credibility in a complex, regulated industry. You can earn the trust of practitioners, distinguish genuine insight from noise, and make product decisions that hold up under scrutiny. Insurance experience is a differentiator, but not required so long as you’re willing to learn the industry quickly.
You work directly alongside engineers and use AI coding tools every day. You understand enough of the architecture (data pipelines, scoring models, LLM evaluation, agentic workflow design) to hold informed technical opinions and drive architectural trade-offs.
You are comfortable in enterprise sales environments. You can construct a compelling ROI case, work alongside client partners in an active deal, and support the sale by making customers excited to work with you and watch your roadmap come to fruition.
You have the discipline to stop work that is not driving the expected results. You define success criteria before you build, test early, and have the honesty to pause investments where the data doesn’t support a path forward.
You have the wisdom to balance the work that will keep your existing customers happy and help attract the next customer segment to keep your product’s growth trajectory strong.
You establish strong relationships with your customers and internal stakeholders that allow you to help understand what matters most and to garner the support you need to make tough calls and tradeoffs.

jobs.description:
About Onfleet

Onfleet is the last-mile delivery platform behind millions of deliveries every month for thousands of businesses around the world. We enable shippers to manage deliveries across their private fleet, carriers, and couriers. We make it easy for dispatchers to plan and run their operations, drivers to execute deliveries, and recipients to get real-time tracking and notifications. Our customers span grocery, prepared meals, pharmacy, flowers, furniture, and more.

The Role

We're looking for a Vice President of Product
to lead Product at Onfleet, owning how our strategy gets translated into roadmaps and how roadmaps turn into shipped, adopted products. Your job is to sharpen our strategy where needed and define how the Onfleet product suite evolves as we scale up in a fast-growing market. This is a hands-on leadership seat where you'll stay close to the details and roll up your sleeves when the team needs it.

You'll report to our CEO and lead Product Management, Design, and User Research. You’ll also work closely with Engineering, QA, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Experience. As our senior-most product leader, you'll sit on our Strategic Leadership Team and represent Product in company planning.

What You'll Do

Own the product roadmap that delivers on our strategy, and update both as our market and target customers change.
Prioritize aggressively by committing to a few well-scoped bets per quarter and saying no to other competing initiatives.
Build deep knowledge of the last-mile delivery industry and our core users: shippers, carriers and couriers, dispatchers, drivers, and recipients.
Lead quarterly and annual planning with Engineering and go-to-market leaders, and partner with them to set company goals that tie product work to business outcomes.
Own how we gather, prioritize, and close the loop on product feedback from customers, Sales, CX, and other internal teams.
Coordinate work across squads so dependencies and risks surface early, and keep one roadmap view the whole company can see.
Connect product success metrics to company metrics, and build a team habit of defining success before launch and acting on what adoption data shows.
Represent Product internally and with our board of directors, customer advisory boards, and key customers.
Foster a collaborative team culture and think ahead about team structure, process, and tooling.
Coach the team and define clear growth paths for each member.

What You'll Bring

You have 10+ years in B2B SaaS product roles, including 5+ years leading product teams and 3+ years as Director of Product or above.
You've run Product at a Series B+ company generating tens of millions of dollars in ARR.
You've led a product through a move upmarket into enterprise.
You've directly hired, managed, and developed Product Managers, Designers, and User Researchers.
You have significant UX and design experience, and you champion it across the company. You've overseen teams that run usability tests, user interviews, and experiments.
You've partnered with Engineering as equals: scoping work together before committing, keeping scope stable once work starts, and shipping in small iterations.
You've run market research to size opportunities in a customer base and adjacent markets.
You make roadmap calls by weighing customer evidence, usage data, strategy, and business impact, and you explain the trade-offs clearly.
You're analytical, using data to make decisions and hold yourself and your team to the numbers.
You've built or managed a Product Operations function, with working fluency in tools like Jira, Productboard, and Amplitude.
You communicate clearly in writing and in person.
You're highly organized and focused on outcomes.

Nice To Have

Experience in last-mile logistics or delivery.

What We Offer

Remote-first work environment with quarterly domestic travel
Generous employee stock options
Comprehensive health, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance
401(k)
Flexible PTO

Onfleet's culture is one that strongly values diversity in its workplace and we are committed to working with potential team members who can bring diverse perspectives and experience to our company and culture.

The Financial Systems Implementation Lead is responsible for leading the successful deployment of enterprise financial systems across planning, configuration, integration, testing, data readiness, deployment, and adoption. This role serves as a critical liaison between Finance, business stakeholders, Digital Technology teams, implementation partners, and functional workstreams to ensure solutions are delivered on time, within scope, and aligned to business objectives.

The role requires a hands-on implementation leader who can translate strategic objectives into practical, scalable solutions while driving cross-functional alignment, issue resolution, and business readiness.

The ideal candidate brings deep implementation experience, strong finance and business process knowledge, structured project delivery skills, and the ability to influence stakeholders in a global, matrixed environment. Program & Project Delivery

Lead financial systems implementation workstreams from planning through deployment, stabilization, and hypercare.
Partner with Finance, business stakeholders, Digital Technology, vendors, and implementation partners to define scope, objectives, requirements, and success criteria.
Develop and manage implementation plans, timelines, dependencies, risks, mitigation strategies, and key delivery milestones.
Coordinate cross-functional execution across business, technology, vendor, and project teams to maintain alignment and accountability.
Monitor project progress, communicate status, and escalate risks, issues, and decisions to leadership and stakeholders.

Coordinate with vendors, implementation partners, and system integrators to ensure solution delivery activities are completed with quality and accountability.

Oversee cutover planning, deployment readiness reviews, go-live execution, and post-go-live support.
Ensure a disciplined transition into production operations, including support readiness, knowledge transfer, and stabilization activities.

Establish and enforce controls to ensure data accuracy, completeness, integrity, and auditability.
Partner with Finance, business, and technology teams to resolve data quality issues and confirm ownership of remediation actions.
Validate migrated data, coordinate reconciliation activities, and support formal business sign-off processes.

Drive stakeholder engagement, adoption, and sustained usage of new processes and technologies across impacted teams.

Identify implementation risks, control considerations, escalation needs, and decision points that may affect scope, timeline, quality, or adoption.

Experience with SAP S/4HANA, Central Finance (CFIN), SAP Group Reporting, SAP BTP, or similar enterprise finance platforms.

jobs.description:
1Password is growing.
We’ve surpassed $400M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Product, the Director of Product, AI Growth grows 1Password's new business in artificial intelligence. In this role, you own driving growth for our AI opportunities by identifying which customers we target, which outcomes we win on, and proving it with design customers. You scale growth through our go-to-market organization and through partnerships with the agent ecosystem and channel partners.

How We’re Using AI Today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

What We're Looking For

Minimum of 8 years of product management experience, including experience carrying a revenue or adoption target, with a preference for experience in security products, agentic products, or developer tools.
Experience owning the strategy for a new product area or market entry, and taking it from hypothesis to customers running in production.
Experience working directly with enterprise customers on a technical deployment, as the person accountable for the outcome, and turning what those deployments proved into a repeatable motion a sales team can run.
Experience building technology partnerships and integrations, including judging where a product should sit in a larger technology ecosystem and working with business development on commercial terms.
Technical depth to hold a credible conversation with developers and security architects about how AI agents are built, deployed, and given access to systems.
Demonstrated ability to build alignment across go-to-market and engineering teams toward a shared goal, without direct authority over either.
Demonstrated ability to make decisions and move work forward with incomplete information in a fast-changing market.
Takes ownership end to end, including the work that falls between teams.
Works AI-first: uses agents in daily work, and applies their own judgement to decisions, product taste, and customer and internal relationships.
Preferred: familiarity with agentic access products, meaning the products that give AI agents credentials and access to the systems they work in.

What You Can Expect

Growth strategy

Own the growth thesis for 1Password's AI opportunities, covering the customer segments we target, the outcomes we deliver that we win on, and the workflows we get embedded into. Revise it as evidence arrives from customers, partners, and the market.
Form and test hypotheses using customer feedback, product usage data, partner input, and market research gathered with the go-to-market, product, user experience, and product marketing teams.
Lead a weekly business review that brings the voice of the customer, field feedback, and product usage telemetry into one view, so the team can refine targets, forecast the roadmap's impact on growth, and prioritize the blockers that hold adoption back.
Identify what stops customers from adopting, and drive each blocker to a resolution with the product team that owns it.

Design customer program

Run the design customer program for new artificial intelligence opportunities, from selecting customers through to delivered outcomes.
Act as the general contractor for each design customer: the single person accountable for getting that customer deployed on 1Password for their agentic access, and for delivering the security and convenience outcomes they came for. Coordinate every team the deployment touches, and build what it requires together with a forward deployed engineering team.
Bring in solutions engineering, customer success, and product managers to help each customer reach their goal, and run feature betas with the product managers who own those features.
Turn what the program proves into the repeatable signal the company needs to scale, meaning the customer evidence, the deployment pattern, and the measured outcomes that the go-to-market and channel teams build sales plays on.
Improve the program each cycle so it reaches more design customers, raises delivery success rates and customer satisfaction, and shortens the time it takes the company to commercialize a new product.

Partnerships

Decide where 1Password should play in the customer's artificial intelligence stack to deliver the most customer value in securing agent access. Agent access can be controlled at several points in that stack, so weigh those points and choose the ones that solve the most of the customer's problem, rather than the ones we fit into most easily. Base the call on how customers run AI today and on how the industry is evolving.
Identify and pursue the partnerships that let us play at those points and that complete an end-to-end customer outcome, meaning the outcome a customer cannot reach with 1Password alone.
Work with partners to deliver integrations, and find the patterns that let us repeat an integration across similar partners instead of building each one from scratch.
Work with the business development team to structure commercial relationships that grow both companies' business and deliver value to shared customers.

Scale through the field and the developer community

Work with product enablement to build demos and enablement content that the field and our channel partners can use without your involvement.
Work with developer relations to grow adoption organically among developers, through reference architectures, sample code, and open source contributions.

Travel

Travel to design customer sites, partner meetings, and industry events approximately 10 to 20% of a given year.

USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $238,000 USD and $357,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $208,000 CAD and $312,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Our culture

At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone . Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.

How We Work With AI

We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

Our approach to remote work

We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events.

What We Offer

We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer:

👶 Maternity and parental leave top-up programs

🩺 Competitive health benefits

🏝 Generous PTO policy

📈 RSU program for most employees

💸 Retirement matching program

🔑 Free 1Password account

Community

🤝 Paid volunteer days

🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly

🌎 Remote-first work environment

Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting.

You belong here.

1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Be yourself, find your people and share the things you love.

Merkle is a leading data-driven, technology-enabled, global performance marketing agency that delivers unique, personalized customer experiences across platforms and devices. About The Role

As Vice President, Client Partner, you are the senior-most Merkle executive on the account. You carry the account’s commercial result, set its strategy, and hold the client relationship at the altitude where budget decisions are made. Every other Merkle function on the account—account management, delivery, solutioning, and sales—contributes to a plan you own.

You will lead a portfolio of strategic accounts generating $5M to $30M+ in annual net revenue across Merkle’s integrated capabilities: Modern CRM, Content Supply Chain, Martech for Media, Connected CX, B2B Transformation, and AI & Agentic Services, supported by alliance partnerships with Adobe, Google, Salesforce, AWS, and Braze, and the full power of One Merkle + One dentsu.

The mandate is deliberate in its order: retention precedes growth. An account that is expanding while its base erodes is not growing. You are measured on the health and defense of the existing book before the increment. That means re-underwriting the value of current work every quarter—not just at renewal—then extending into adjacent scope where Merkle’s delivered performance is already the evidence, and finally opening new buying centers and capabilities with the Enterprise Sales Lead.

You are not an account manager, a delivery leader, or a sales lead. Account management administers the commercial mechanics you direct. Delivery owns method and quality; you set the outcome and the commercial envelope. The Enterprise Sales Lead originates against the strategy you set. The client should be able to name one Merkle executive accountable for their account, and that executive should be able to answer any commercial, relationship, or delivery question about it without deferring. Where the client routes around the Client Partner, the role is not being performed.

This is a remote opportunity that requires regularly being onsite at the client location that is based in Princeton, NJ. Reports to the SVP, Growth Officer.

Responsibilities

Own a portfolio of strategic accounts end-to-end: client satisfaction, revenue retention (>90%), margin quality, forecast accuracy, and year-over-year growth
Defend the contracted revenue base against scope erosion, in-housing, offshore substitution, procurement-driven rate compression, and competitive displacement—re-underwriting the value case quarterly, not annually
Drive revenue expansion through cross-sell, adjacent-scope extension, new buying center entry, and AOR expansion, with at least two qualified non-CXM opportunities per book in support of the One dentsu growth model
Set and own the account strategy and growth plan, ensuring account management, delivery, and the Enterprise Sales Lead are working to a single, current, written plan you chair
Hold executive relationships personally at the altitude where budget decisions are made—CMO, CIO, CFO, and their direct reports—and map stakeholder coverage so that no single departure creates material account risk
Navigate complex multi-stakeholder environments across business, technology, operations, vendor management, and procurement, adapting your approach to each buyer style and extending Merkle’s footprint up and across the client organization

Bridge sub-Practice delivery with Solutioning, Account, and Program Management to streamline execution and deliver a white-glove client experience, holding delivery accountable for method and quality while you hold the commercial result
Partner with Alliance leaders (Adobe, Google, Salesforce, AWS, Braze) on joint account planning, pipeline mapping, and co-sell motions—bringing at least one Alliance Joint Teaming motion per account growth plan annually
Run a proactive Client Partner cadence: Innovation Days, Discovery Workshops, Executive Business Reviews, and quarterly value reviews structured around measured outcomes rather than activity
Maintain a frequent, consistent stream of thought leadership into your accounts—events, POVs, workshops, and executive narratives that position Merkle as a strategic partner, not a vendor
Provide leadership and direction to Account Directors, Engagement Leaders, and Capability teams in a matrixed environment, ensuring the account team operates as one seamless unit

CLIENT CHALLENGES YOU’LL SOLVE

Client Partners at Merkle operate at the intersection of strategy and execution. Your portfolio will span clients facing transformation challenges that require integrated thinking across data, technology, and customer experience. You’ll build account strategies—and create opportunities for clients to think more broadly about Merkle’s capabilities—around problems like these:

Unifying fragmented customer data and CRM systems to power personalization, loyalty, and orchestrated journeys across every channel—replacing siloed point solutions with a connected experience architecture
Scaling content production without scaling headcount, using AI to accelerate creation, manage assets, and streamline creative operations across markets and channels
Transforming B2B go-to-market from siloed marketing and sales into integrated, account-based motions with measurable pipeline impact and closed-loop attribution
Deploying AI and agentic automation across the customer experience—conversational interfaces, adaptive commerce, intelligent service—to drive engagement and operational efficiency simultaneously
Defending marketing investment against CFO scrutiny by building enterprise measurement and analytics capabilities that tie experience spend to revenue outcomes the finance function will accept
Navigating platform migrations and martech rationalization—helping clients move from legacy stacks to modern, composable architectures without disrupting the customer experience in flight

THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE WILL BRING

15+ years of progressive experience in client services, client management, or enterprise account leadership within an advertising agency, consultancy, marketing services firm, systems integrator, or client-side marketing organization, with direct P&L accountability for accounts of meaningful scale
Demonstrated success owning $20M+ books and leading complex, multi-service-line engagements across multiple industries, with a track record that includes both growing and defending revenue under pressure
Executive relationships held personally at CMO, CIO, or CFO level—not inherited or brokered—with the presence and credibility to earn trust at the altitude where budget decisions are made
Deep working knowledge of CXM/CRM, Loyalty, Data and Analytics, Identity, Digital Marketing, Content Supply Chain, B2B, and Enterprise AI / Martech—sufficient to hold a substantive conversation with a client technology leader, not just name the categories
Experience directing account teams you do not line-manage, and the judgment to set direction without relying on escalation—comfortable being accountable for outcomes produced by people who do not report to you
Strong commercial acumen: pricing strategy, multi-year deal structuring, negotiation, margin defense against procurement, and the discipline to manage forecasts, contracts, and AR with rigor
A specific account you defended against in-housing, offshore substitution, or a competitive displacement attempt—with the story of how you did it
Working command of modern AI capability and its effect on delivery timelines, commercial models, and client expectations
Alliance experience with Adobe, Salesforce, or a comparable platform partner, including joint account planning and co-sell execution
Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree a plus

What Success Looks Like

In your first 30 days, you’ve taken full handover of the commercial position, contract terms, delivery status, and relationship map for your portfolio. You’ve met every named client stakeholder and identified the retention risks nobody has written down
By day 60, you’ve published the account plan for each account and established the operating cadence. Account management, delivery, and the Enterprise Sales Lead are working to it. You’ve agreed the annual commitment with the SVP, Growth Officer
By day 90, you hold executive relationships at least one level above your predecessor’s highest contact. You’ve closed or addressed the most urgent retention exposure and opened at least one extension opportunity in your largest account
By month six, you’ve completed one renewal on improved terms, produced a client-attested value result, and have a qualified pipeline of growth opportunities across your book that reflects the full breadth of Merkle’s capabilities

1Password is growing.
We’ve surpassed $400M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Product, the Director of Product, AI Growth grows 1Password's new business in artificial intelligence. In this role, you own driving growth for our AI opportunities by identifying which customers we target, which outcomes we win on, and proving it with design customers. You scale growth through our go-to-market organization and through partnerships with the agent ecosystem and channel partners.

How We’re Using AI Today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

What We're Looking For

Minimum of 8 years of product management experience, including experience carrying a revenue or adoption target, with a preference for experience in security products, agentic products, or developer tools.
Experience owning the strategy for a new product area or market entry, and taking it from hypothesis to customers running in production.
Experience working directly with enterprise customers on a technical deployment, as the person accountable for the outcome, and turning what those deployments proved into a repeatable motion a sales team can run.
Experience building technology partnerships and integrations, including judging where a product should sit in a larger technology ecosystem and working with business development on commercial terms.
Technical depth to hold a credible conversation with developers and security architects about how AI agents are built, deployed, and given access to systems.
Demonstrated ability to build alignment across go-to-market and engineering teams toward a shared goal, without direct authority over either.
